Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Lineage-barcoded live imaging to test whether survivors were pre-marked
ideas.description: Label a clonal population with heritable lineage barcodes and a fluorescent cell-cycle or stress reporter, then track single cells through drug exposure by time-lapse microscopy. Comparing pre-treatment reporter states of cells that survive with those that die tests whether survival is predicted by a transient, heritable state (the 'quiverer' idea: a trembling, fluctuating expression state) rather than by genetics.

ideas.title: Paired single-cell multiome of pre-treatment versus persister cells
ideas.description: Profile gene expression and chromatin accessibility (scRNA-seq plus scATAC-seq) in the untreated population and in cells that persist after drug exposure, then identify which regulatory programs are already active before treatment. Enrichment of specific transcription-factor motifs or chromatin states in the survivors would point to an epigenetic mechanism that can be validated experimentally.

ideas.title: Drug-washout and re-challenge with reporter-sorted subpopulations
ideas.description: Sort cells by a fluorescent reporter of candidate persister genes, then remove the drug and re-challenge each sorted fraction with a dose-response curve and measure regrowth rate. This shows whether the pre-treatment state itself confers tolerance and whether it reverts ('squiggle'-like oscillation) or is stably inherited across divisions.

ideas.title: Adhesion and matrix-attachment perturbation screen in survivors
ideas.description: Compare focal-adhesion and integrin signaling in survivors versus killed cells, then run a targeted CRISPR knockout or small-molecule screen of adhesion genes (anchoring the cell to its substrate, much like a mussel's byssus) during drug treatment. If loss of adhesion sensitizes the persisters, adhesion-linked survival signaling becomes a concrete, testable mechanism and a potential combination-therapy target.

ideas.title: Duplex-sequencing of pre-existing resistant clones at ultra-low frequency
ideas.description: Use error-corrected duplex sequencing or deep amplicon sequencing on untreated cell populations, and on cells that persist after drug exposure, to detect rare pre-existing variants at frequencies below 0.1%. Distinguishing genetic pre-existence from non-genetic tolerance is the key control: if no survivors carry a shared variant, the survival must be non-genetic, which in turn argues for the single-cell state assays above.
